newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank merger foes seek longer comment.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank merger foes seek longer comment.

text.p: Inner City Press/Community on the Move said Monday it was seeking a 60-day extension of the period allowed for public comment on the proposed acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc by NationsBank Corp.
The Bronx, N.Y., community group has previously filed applications with bank regulators urging denial of the combination.

The request for the extension, in effect a doubling of the usual 60-day period, was included in the group's third comment filed with the Federal Reserve Board and the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond since the merger announcement.

In a news release accompanying Inner City's filing, the group said it had additional documentation for its challenges to the merger on grounds of antitrust and interstate banking law. It also said it had more documentation for its allegations that NationsBank had engaged in predatory lending through its NationsCredit consumer finance subsidiary.

Asked for comment, Jan Boylston, senior vice president for corporate affairs at Charlotte, N.C.-based NationsBank, said the company had not seen the latest comment but believed that its community investment record would withstand scrutiny.
"We've been a leader in increased lending in both minority markets and low and moderate-income neighborhoods," Boylston said.

She said NationsBank had lent $13.4 billion in community development programs from 1992 to 1995, beating a $10 billion pledge it made at the beginning of the period. She said that figure did not include any lending by NationsCredit.

Asked to comment on Inner City's contention that a NationsBank "presence" in New Mexico should keep the transaction from being approved, Boylston said the bank had no significant presence in that state.
She said the company had purchased a small El Paso, Texas-based bank that operates a single branch in nearby New Mexico.

In its comments, Inner City has cited a U.S. law that says a merger should not be approved if it would give the acquirer 30 percent of the deposits in a state where the target is located. St. Louis-based Boatmen's and its units have more than a 30 percent share in New Mexico. The provision of the law exempts acquirers that do not already have a presence in the state in question.
The proposed acquisition of Boatmen's by NationsBank is valued at about $9 billion.
The merger was proposed August 30, and the initial comment period will end November 4. The banks are seeking to complete the transaction in early January.
